title: Badr: the night rain
hookLine: before Badr, Allah sends sleep for calm and rain to firm the ground (8:11)

cards: The night before a fight the Muslims hadn't set out for. They had ridden out of Medina after a trading caravan from Mecca.

The caravan slipped away along the coast, and instead an army from Mecca was coming to meet them, at a place of wells called Badr. Now they're camped in a sandy valley, outnumbered, the battle set for morning.
A night like that is made for lying awake, running through what might happen. Surah eight remembers what happened that night instead. Today: Badr.

teach.b: Surah eight, verse eleven, speaks to the believers about that night. It opens, in Pickthall's words: "When He made the slumber fall upon you as a reassurance from Him."
Slumber: a drowsiness that comes down over anxious people and lets them rest. The verse calls it a reassurance, sent from Allah. Then it goes on: He sent down water from the sky.

teach.h: RAIN TO MAKE THE FEET FIRM.
teach.b: The same verse gives the rain its jobs: to purify them, to take from them a taint of Satan, to strengthen their hearts, and to make their feet firm. Ibn Ishaq fills in the ground-level picture.

The valley was soft sand. The rain packed it down where the Muslims were, so they could walk and stand on it, while the same rain made the going heavy for the army on the other side. Some reports add another picture.
In Musnad Ahmad, Ali says that on the night of Badr everyone slept except the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, who stood praying under a tree until morning.
So the story holds both: a camp of people given sleep, and one man awake on their behalf. Notice the order inside that one verse. It doesn't speak of swords.
It speaks of sleep, then rain, and only then of firm feet. Before anyone is asked to stand, they're given rest, and the ground is made ready for their feet.

how: Muslims read surah al-Anfal (8) for the story of Badr, and some recite the Prophet's bedtime remembrances before sleep.

games.q: badr: the night rain — tap the pairs.

s: in 8:11, slumber and rain come before firm feet
slumber as a reassurance, then water from the sky to make their feet firm.
the rain made the ground muddy for the Muslims
in Ibn Ishaq it packed the sand firm for them.
the Muslims set out from Medina expecting to fight an army
they rode out after a caravan; the army came instead.

games.q: it's the night before a battle you didn't plan for, and you're outnumbered. what does 8:11 say Allah sent that night?
games.why: 8:11 says Allah made slumber fall on them as a reassurance, and sent rain to purify them and make their feet firm.

practice: Think of the next hard day ahead of you, a meeting, an exam, a long shift, and notice the part of you that wants to stay up rehearsing it.

Then picture rain falling on soft sand and packing it firm while you sleep, a part you don't have to do, and breathe out slowly, longer than you breathe in. If you pray, you can ask Allah for calm and for firm ground.

wordCard.voice: Badr. The place of wells where the Muslims camped the night before a great test, and where, the Qur'an says, Allah sent slumber for calm and rain to make their feet firm. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: 'slumber, drowsiness', the word in 8:11 for the sleep that fell on them.

carryVoice: Your line: sleep, then stand. Rest came first, then firm ground, and only then the morning. That's day seven hundred seventy-six.

sources.q: When He made the slumber fall upon you as a reassurance from Him

sources.ref: Qur'an 8:11 (water from the sky to purify, remove a taint of Satan, strengthen hearts, make feet firm)
Ibn Ishaq, Sirat Rasul Allah (the caravan escapes; the rain firms the sand for the Muslims and hampers Quraysh)
